attributes.nuance_translation: A phrase used when a specific event will go on to occur, or continue to intensify.

attributes.body:
This grammar construction is a mix of the conjunction particle て, and the verb 行（い）く 'to go'. To use this grammar point, you will need to attach て to any verb, and then follow it with いく.

This nuance is usually that '(A) happened and then went', or 'will happen, and then go'. In other words, it will depend on whether いく is in present, or past tense.

ていく can be used when representing time, or when representing a physical place. When representing a physical place, it is more likely that the kanji structure, 行（い）く will be used. However, this is not a set rule, and depends on the writer.

When used in relation to time, the nuance is usually that something has already started/is about to start, and then will continue to progress in the same way.

This is the opposite of てくる, which indicates that something has finally reached a certain state, after progressing in that way for some time.

Fun Fact

When compared to English, ていく is very similar to the phrase 'to go on to (A)', in relation to time. It focuses on the fact that the speaker is required to make some type of journey to arrive at a specific point. For example, 'She went on to become a doctor after university'.

attributes.source: [DBJG] A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar
[AIAIJ] An Integrated Approach to Intermediate Japanese

attributes.description: Using motion verbs （行く、来る） with the te-form
Helping Verbs: …ていく and …てくる

attributes.body: てくる and ていく combine the て-form of a verb with 来る or 行く to express movement or change over time. てくる suggests movement toward the speaker or a change that started in the past and leads up to now. ていく implies movement away from the speaker or a change that begins now and continues into the future.

second_relatable.title: ていく

attributes.body: The verb いく expresses movement in a direction, literally or figuratively. へいく is used after nouns to indicate moving toward a place (e.g., 学校へいく = 'go to school'). When used as ていく (Verb + て + いく), it implies a continuing action or change moving forward. Note that いく is written in kanji as 行く when used alone, but typically in hiragana in the ていく form.

first_relatable.title: へいく
first_relatable.meaning: To go to, To head toward

second_relatable.title: ていく
second_relatable.meaning: To ~ and go, To go on, To start

attributes.body: Verb + にいく combines the verb stem with にいく to express going somewhere to do something (e.g., 食べに行く = 'go to eat'). In contrast, ていく (Verb + て + いく) expresses sequential actions (e.g., 食べて行く = 'eat, then go') or actions that progress over time (e.g., 上手くなっていく = 'get better over time').

first_relatable.title: Verb + にいく
first_relatable.meaning: To go ~, To go in order to ~

second_relatable.title: ていく
second_relatable.meaning: To ~ and go, To go on, To start

attributes.body: ていく expresses either literal movement away from the speaker or a change that begins now and continues into the future. In contrast, はじめる attaches to the verb stem to mean 'to start (A)'. The key difference is nuance: ていく highlights ongoing progression and continuation going forward, while はじめる focuses on the starting point and the idea of commencing an action.
